dc11.title: Notification toggles
dc11.summary: A team-chat settings page. Make seven notification rows switchable, show a derived "4 of 7 enabled" count, and wire "Turn all off".
dc11.brief:
Tandem’s notification settings page is laid out but the rows are read-only. App.tsx has Sidebar, DoNotDisturbCard and NotificationsCard. The seven settings come from data/notifications.ts (4 of them start enabled).

Read components/Toggle.tsx first: it is a controlled switch (checked + onChange(next)), and DoNotDisturbCard already shows how to use it. Reuse it; don’t build a new switch. No API in this one.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3, and the change.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The list of settings becomes state in NotificationsCard, initialised from DEFAULT_SETTINGS. Toggling one is a map that returns a new object for the matching id. The count is derived with filter(...).length, so it can never get out of sync. "Turn all off" is another map setting every enabled to false."
requirements: Each of the 7 rows shows the existing <Toggle /> on the right, reflecting that setting’s enabled value. Clicking it flips only that row
Under "Notify me about" the header shows "4 of 7 enabled" on load and updates on every toggle. It is derived from the list, not a separate counter
Turn all off switches every row off ("0 of 7 enabled"). Disabled rows show their label in the muted color

change.title: Turn all back on
change.html:
"Users who hit Turn all off can’t find a way back."

  • When 0 settings are enabled, the button reads Turn all on and switches all 7 on. Otherwise it reads Turn all off.

Hint: the label and the target value are both decided from the derived count, above the return.

hints: State placement: only NotificationsCard needs the list, so useState(DEFAULT_SETTINGS) goes there.
Type it: useState<NotificationSetting[]>(DEFAULT_SETTINGS) with import type { NotificationSetting } from "./data/notifications";
Never change the object in place. Search: "react updating arrays in state" (react.dev has a page on it).
Toggle one: setSettings((prev) => { return prev.map((s) => { if (s.id !== id) { return s; } return { ...s, enabled: next }; }); });
Count: const enabledCount = settings.filter((s) => { return s.enabled; }).length; above the return.
rubric: Reused Toggle instead of writing a new switch
One array in state (not seven booleans)
Updates are immutable (map + spread), using the updater form
Count derived, not stored
Bulk action is one map over the list
Label/target decided above the return, no ternaries in JSX

primitives.name: map() to update one item
primitives.syntax: list.map((x) => { if (x.id !== id) { return x; } return { ...x, done: true }; })
primitives.example:
[{id:'a',on:false},{id:'b',on:false}].map((x) => { if (x.id !== 'b') { return x; } return { ...x, on: true }; })
// [{id:'a',on:false},{id:'b',on:true}]
primitives.note: Returns a new array of the same length. Return the old item untouched for the others and a new object for the one you change. Never assign x.on = true: that mutates state.

primitives.name: Object spread
primitives.example:
const s = { id: 'dm', enabled: true };
({ ...s, enabled: false })   // { id: 'dm', enabled: false }  (s is unchanged)
primitives.note: Returns a new object: a shallow copy with the listed keys overridden. Keys written after the spread win.

primitives.name: Count with filter().length
primitives.example: [{on:true},{on:false},{on:true}].filter((x) => { return x.on; }).length   // 2
primitives.note: filter returns a new array of the items where the callback returned true; .length counts them. Derive counts like this instead of keeping a counter in state.

primitives.name: useState updater form
primitives.example: setCount((prev) => { return prev + 1; });   // always uses the latest value
primitives.note: Pass a function when the new state depends on the old one. React calls it with the current value and stores what you return.

dc12.title: Pricing: billing toggle
dc12.summary: A dark pricing page for a video editor. Wire the Monthly/Yearly switch (yearly = 2 months free), plan selection, and per-card "Show all features".
dc12.brief:
Framecut’s pricing page renders three PlanCards from data/plans.ts, plus a BillingToggle that looks right but does nothing. Prices are stored in cents as a monthly price.

Read utils/formatPrice.ts first: it already turns cents into "$12", "$24.17" or "Free". Reuse it for every number you show. No API in this one.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Stretch: 5.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Billing and the selected plan are needed by every card and by the toggle, so both live in App and go down as props. Whether a card’s feature list is expanded only matters to that card, so that is local state in PlanCard. The yearly price is derived: monthlyCents * 10, never stored."
requirements: Clicking Monthly / Yearly switches billing. The active option gets the white pill (is-active). Monthly is the default
Monthly: paid plans show "$12" + "/month". Yearly: they show the yearly total, monthly × 10: "$120" + "/year" (Studio "$290"). Hobby always shows "Free" with no period. All via formatPrice
Yearly also shows a muted line under the price: "$10/mo, billed yearly" (Studio: "$24.17/mo, billed yearly"). Not shown for Hobby or on Monthly
Clicking Choose Creator selects that plan: the card gets a purple border + glow (is-selected) and the button reads Selected ✓. Only one plan is selected at a time
Each card’s Show all N features expands just that card’s list and becomes Show less. Other cards stay as they are
hints: Two kinds of state: shared (billing, selectedId in App) and local (expanded in PlanCard). Ask "who needs to know?"
Type the billing: type Billing = "monthly" | "yearly"; then useState<Billing>("monthly").
Decide the price above the return: let amount = formatPrice(plan.monthlyCents); if (!isFree && billing === "yearly") { amount = formatPrice(plan.monthlyCents * 10); ... }
Per month on yearly: formatPrice(Math.round(yearlyCents / 12)). Search: "mdn Math.round" if you want to see why not toFixed here.
Expand: let shown = plan.features.slice(0, 3); if (expanded) { shown = plan.features; }
rubric: Shared state in App, expand state local to the card (said why)
Prices derived from monthlyCents, nothing duplicated in state
Reused formatPrice everywhere
Free plan handled without special-casing in JSX
Selected stored as an id
Class names and labels built above the return

primitives.name: String literal union type
primitives.note: A type that only allows the listed strings. Use it instead of a boolean like isYearly when the options have names.

primitives.name: Typing a callback prop
primitives.syntax: type Props = { value: Billing; onChange: (next: Billing) => void };
primitives.example: function BillingToggle({ value, onChange }: Props) { ... onChange('yearly'); ... }
primitives.note: (next: Billing) => void means "a function that takes a Billing and returns nothing". The parent owns the state; the child only calls onChange.

primitives.name: Money in cents
primitives.note: Keep money as integer cents and only format at the edge. Integer maths is exact; decimal dollars are not.

dc13.title: Courses: loading, error, empty
dc13.summary: A learning app’s "My learning" page. Load courses per tab with skeleton cards, an error panel with Retry, and an empty state.
dc13.brief:
Learnloop’s "My learning" page has a header, working tabs (In progress / Completed / Wishlist) and a dev-only Simulate failure checkbox. CourseList receives status and shouldFail but renders nothing yet.

Read api.ts: getCourses(status, shouldFail) takes 0.4–1.2 s, rejects when shouldFail is true, and returns an empty array for the wishlist. components/CourseCard.tsx already renders one course and components/SkeletonCard.tsx its grey placeholder; reuse both. The CSS for skeletons and the .state-panel / .primary-btn classes is already in styles.css, so this one is all React.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Stretch: 5.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"CourseList owns courses, loading and error. One effect depends on status and shouldFail: it sets loading, calls the API, and handles .then and .catch, with a cancelled flag so a slow old tab can’t overwrite a new one. For Retry I add an attempt counter to the dependencies and bump it. Rendering is four early returns: loading, error, empty, list."
requirements: On first load and on every tab change, show 3 skeleton cards (reuse components/SkeletonCard) until the API answers, then a CourseCard per course
With Simulate failure checked, the request fails and the list shows an error panel (.state-panel.is-error): "Couldn’t load your courses.", a short help line, and a Retry button
Retry shows the skeletons again and re-requests (still failing while the box is checked; uncheck it and the courses load)
The Wishlist tab (empty array) shows an empty state (.state-panel): "No courses here yet", a help line and a Browse catalog button. Never a blank area
Clicking tabs quickly never shows the wrong tab’s courses (ignore responses from an effect that has been cleaned up)
hints: Three pieces of state: useState<Course[]>([]), loading (start true) and useState<string | null>(null) for the error.
Errors from a Promise go to .catch. Search: "mdn Promise catch".
Retry without duplicating the fetch: const [attempt, setAttempt] = useState(0); put attempt in the effect’s dependency array, and Retry does setAttempt((prev) => { return prev + 1; });
Start of the effect: let cancelled = false; setLoading(true); setError(null); and in both .then and .catch: if (cancelled) { return; }

Render with early returns above the main JSX: if (loading) { return <div className="course-grid"><SkeletonCard /><SkeletonCard /><SkeletonCard /></div>; }, then if (error), then if (courses.length === 0).
rubric: Effect depends on status + shouldFail (+ retry counter)
Both then and catch end loading
Error cleared and loading set when re-requesting
Cancelled flag in cleanup
Reused CourseCard
Empty state is distinct from loading and error
Skeleton matches the card’s shape

primitives.name: .then() / .catch()
primitives.example:
getCourses('wishlist', true)
  .then((data) => { setCourses(data); })
  .catch((err) => { setError('Couldn’t load your courses.'); });   // runs: it rejected
primitives.note: .then runs when the promise resolves, .catch when it rejects (a thrown error). Turn loading off in both, or a failure spins forever.

primitives.name: useEffect dependency array
primitives.example: useEffect(() => { load(status); }, [status]);   // runs on mount, then again whenever status changes
primitives.note: The effect re-runs after any render where a listed value changed. List every prop/state the effect reads. An empty [] means "once, on mount".

primitives.name: Early return for UI states
primitives.note: A component can return different JSX before the main return. Order matters: check loading, then error, then empty, then the list. Hooks must all be called above the first early return.

primitives.name: State that can be null
primitives.example:
const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
if (error) { /* here TS knows error is a string */ }
primitives.note: The union string | null says "a message, or nothing yet". An if (error) check narrows it to string.

dc14.title: Shop: category chips
dc14.summary: A plant shop grid. Load categories from the API, show filter chips with product counts and an "All" chip, and filter the grid.
dc14.brief:
Fernwood’s product grid already loads and renders: ProductGrid fetches with getProducts() and maps to ProductCard. The Figma adds a row of category chips between the heading and the grid.

Read api.ts: getCategories() returns names but no counts (0.3–0.9 s; products take 0.5–1.2 s). Think about where the products have to live once the chips need to count them.

components/Chip.tsx is the pill button from the design system (label, count bubble, active, disabled), and its CSS is already in styles.css. You only lay out the row.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The chips need the products to count them and the grid needs them to render, so the products move up into a parent (Catalog) along with the categories and activeCategory. I load both with Promise.all so there’s one loading state. Counts and the visible list are derived with filter. ProductGrid becomes a plain component that just receives the visible products."
requirements: Above the grid, a Chip (reuse components/Chip.tsx) per category from getCategories(), preceded by an All chip. Each chip shows its product count: "All 12", "Indoor plants 5", "Pots 4", "Plant care 3", "Gift cards 0"
Clicking a chip filters the grid to that category; All shows everything. The active chip is filled dark green with white text (is-active). All is active on load
Chips and grid appear together after both requests finish ("Loading the greenhouse…" until then)
A chip with a count of 0 (Gift cards) is disabled and faded (pass disabled to Chip)
hints: This is "lifting state up": move products out of ProductGrid into a parent that renders both the chips and the grid.
Two requests, one loading state. Search: "mdn Promise.all". Promise.all([getProducts(), getCategories()]).then(([products, categories]) => { ... })
Count for a chip: products.filter((p) => { return p.categoryId === c.id; }).length
Use a constant for All: const ALL = "all"; and useState(ALL). Visible list: let visible = products; if (active !== ALL) { visible = products.filter(...); }
components/Chip.tsx already takes label, count, active, disabled and onClick: render one for All and one per category inside a <div className="chips">.
rubric: Recognised that products must be lifted
Loaded both endpoints with one loading state
Counts derived, not fetched or stored
Active category stored as an id
Reused ProductCard / formatPrice untouched
Disabled empty chip
cancelled guard kept

primitives.name: Promise.all
primitives.note: Starts both requests at once and resolves with an array of results in the same order once all have finished. If any one rejects, the whole thing rejects.

primitives.name: Array destructuring
primitives.example:
const [products, categories] = [['p1', 'p2'], ['plants']];
products     // ['p1', 'p2']
primitives.note: Unpacks an array by position into named variables. Works in parameters too: .then(([a, b]) => ...).

primitives.name: filter() by a field
primitives.example: [{c:'pots'},{c:'plants'},{c:'pots'}].filter((p) => { return p.c === 'pots'; })   // 2 items
primitives.note: Returns a new array with the matching items (possibly empty). Use it for both the visible list and, with .length, the counts.

primitives.name: Lifting state up
primitives.syntax: // move the state to the closest common parent, pass it down as props
primitives.example:
function Catalog() { const [products, setProducts] = useState<Product[]>([]); ...
  return <><Chips products={products} /><ProductGrid products={visible} /></>; }
primitives.note: When two siblings need the same data, the state moves up to their parent and both receive it as props. The child that used to fetch becomes a plain component.

dc15.title: Transactions: sortable table
dc15.summary: A business-banking transactions table. Make the headers sort by date, text and amount, asc/desc with arrows, without mutating the data.
dc15.brief:
Ledgerly’s transactions page loads and renders a table via getTransactions() (0.3–1.0 s). The rows come back in the order the bank posted them. The headers are plain text.

Read utils/format.ts (formatMoney, formatDate) and the Transaction type: date is an ISO string, amountCents is negative for money out.

components/SortHeader.tsx was built for the Invoices table: give it a direction ("asc", "desc" or null) and an onClick and it renders the header button with ▲/▼. Its base CSS is in styles.css. Your job is the sort state and the sorting.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3, and the change.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Sort state is sortKey (or null) and sortDir, in TransactionsTable next to the data. The sorted list is derived each render from a copy ([...list].sort), so the API order is always still there. One comparator per type: subtraction for amounts, timestamps for dates, localeCompare for text. A SortHeader component renders the button and arrow."
requirements: Every header (Date, Description, Category, Amount) is a SortHeader (reuse components/SortHeader.tsx). First click sorts that column ascending (▲), the next click descending (▼). Clicking another column starts it at ascending
Correct per type: Amount numerically (−$14,500.00 is lowest), Date chronologically, Description/Category alphabetically (case-insensitive, localeCompare)
Extend SortHeader: inactive headers show a muted ↕; the active one is green (is-active) with its arrow. The <th> has aria-sort ("ascending" / "descending" / "none")

change.title: Third click clears
change.html:
"Finance wants to get back to the bank’s posted order."

  • A third click on the same column clears sorting: all headers show ↕ and the rows return to the original API order.

If you sorted the state array in place, the original order is gone. That is exactly what this change tests.

hints: .sort() sorts in place and returns the same array. Search: "mdn Array.prototype.sort" (and look at toSorted).
Copy first: const sorted = [...list].sort((a, b) => { return a.amountCents - b.amountCents; });
Dates: new Date(a.date).getTime() - new Date(b.date).getTime(). Text: a.description.localeCompare(b.description).
Descending: sort ascending and then sorted.reverse(). That’s safe because sorted is already your copy.

Click logic: if (column !== sortKey) { setSortKey(column); setSortDir("asc"); return; } setSortDir("desc");. For each header: direction={dirFor("date")} where dirFor returns sortDir for the active column and null otherwise. (The change adds one more branch.)
rubric: Never mutated the loaded array
Sorted list derived, not stored
Right comparator per data type
Arrow and active class decided above the return
Header is a real button (keyboard accessible)
Change done by extending the click logic, not a new flag

primitives.name: sort() with a comparator, on a copy
primitives.syntax: const sorted = [...list].sort((a, b) => { return a.n - b.n; });
primitives.note: sort sorts in place and returns the same array, so copy first ([...list] or list.toSorted(...)). Comparator: negative = a first, positive = b first. Without one, numbers sort as text (10 before 9).

primitives.name: localeCompare()
primitives.example:
'figma'.localeCompare('Amazon')                              // 1  (f after a)
['b','A','c'].sort((x, y) => { return x.localeCompare(y); })   // ['A','b','c']
primitives.note: Returns a negative number, 0 or positive: exactly what a sort comparator needs. Handles case and accents like a human would expect.

primitives.name: Date.getTime()
primitives.example: new Date('2026-09-02').getTime() - new Date('2026-09-14').getTime()   // negative: Sep 2 comes first
primitives.note: Returns milliseconds since 1970 as a number, so dates can be subtracted. (ISO strings like "2026-09-14" also sort correctly as text.)

primitives.name: reverse()
primitives.example:
const copy = [1, 2, 3];
copy.reverse();   // copy is now [3, 2, 1]
primitives.note: Reverses in place (and returns the same array). Fine on your own sorted copy; never on state.

dc16.title: Orders: pagination
dc16.summary: A bakery’s wholesale admin. Page through 23 orders from a paginated API: Prev/Next, page numbers, "Showing 6–10 of 23", disabled at the ends.
dc16.brief:
Crumb & Co.’s order table loads, but OrdersTable always asks for page 1. The API is server-paginated: getOrders(page, pageSize) returns { orders, total } after 0.3–0.9 s. Pages start at 1. There are 23 orders and PAGE_SIZE is 5.

Read api.ts and the existing effect first. You extend it rather than writing a second one.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"page goes in OrdersTable and into the effect’s dependencies, so changing it refetches. pageCount, the first and last row numbers are derived from page, PAGE_SIZE and total. While a new page loads I keep the old rows, dim them, and disable the buttons. A Pagination component gets page, pageCount and onChange."
requirements: Under the table, ← Prev and Next → load the previous/next page. Prev is disabled on page 1, Next on the last page (5)
Left of the buttons: "Showing 6–10 of 23" for page 2, "Showing 1–5 of 23" for page 1, "Showing 21–23 of 23" on the last page
Page number buttons 1–5 between Prev and Next. The current one is filled raspberry and has aria-current="page". Clicking one jumps there
While a page loads, the previous rows stay visible but dimmed (.is-loading) and the pagination buttons are disabled. "Loading orders…" only shows on the very first load
hints: Add const [page, setPage] = useState(1); and change the effect to getOrders(page, PAGE_SIZE) with [page] as dependencies.
Math: pageCount = Math.ceil(total / PAGE_SIZE), first = (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE + 1, last = Math.min(page * PAGE_SIZE, total).
The numbers 1..n: Array.from({ length: pageCount }, (_, i) => { return i + 1; }). Search: "mdn Array.from length".
Set setLoading(true) at the start of the effect but keep orders, so the table doesn’t jump. Only show the full loading message when orders.length === 0.
Disabled flags above the return: const prevDisabled = loading || page === 1;
rubric: Page in the effect dependencies, one effect
Range text and page count derived
Last-page range clamps to total
Prev/Next disabled at the ends
Old rows kept while loading (no layout jump)
cancelled guard kept for fast clicking

primitives.name: Math.ceil() for a page count
primitives.example:
Math.ceil(23 / 5)   // 5  (4.6 rounds UP: the last page has 3 rows)
Math.floor(23 / 5)  // 4
primitives.note: Rounds up to the next whole number. Pages are always rounded up; a partial page is still a page.

primitives.name: Math.min() to clamp
primitives.example:
Math.min(5 * 5, 23)   // 23  (not 25: the last page stops at the total)
Math.min(2 * 5, 23)   // 10
primitives.note: Returns the smallest of its arguments. Use it to cap a value; Math.max sets a floor.

primitives.name: State in the effect’s dependencies
primitives.example: setPage(2);   // render → effect sees page changed → getOrders(2, 5)
primitives.note: Changing page is all a button does; the effect notices the new value and refetches. Don’t call the API from the click handler as well.

primitives.name: disabled buttons
primitives.example: <button disabled={page === 1}>← Prev</button>   // greyed out, no click events, skipped by Tab
primitives.note: A disabled button does not fire onClick, so the handler needs no extra guard. Style it with :disabled.

dc17.title: Sign-up form validation
dc17.summary: An AI writing app’s sign-up. Validate email, show password rules as a live checklist, check confirmation, show errors after blur or submit, then submit async.
dc17.brief:
Northstar’s sign-up page has a brand panel and a form with three controlled inputs inside the existing Field component. Submitting does nothing yet.

Read components/Field.tsx (pass it an error and it renders the red line and border), utils/validate.ts (isValidEmail and PASSWORD_RULES) and api.ts: createAccount takes 0.6–1.2 s and rejects for taken@example.com.

The CSS for the checklist, the API banner and the success panel is already in styles.css, so you can spend the time on the logic.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Stretch: 5.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Errors are derived from the three values on every render, never stored. Whether to show them is separate state: a touched object set on blur, and a submitted flag set on submit. The checklist maps over PASSWORD_RULES. Submit sets submitted, returns if anything is invalid, otherwise sets status to submitting and calls the API; .catch shows the server message, .then swaps to a success panel."
requirements: Under the password, a live checklist of the 3 PASSWORD_RULES: grey ○ when unmet, green ✓ (is-met) as soon as it’s met (styles exist: .rules, .rule)

Submitting (e.preventDefault()) shows the email error: "Email is required" when empty or "Enter a valid email address" when isValidEmail fails, passed to Field’s error. No errors before the first submit, and an invalid form never calls the API

Password shows "Password doesn’t meet all the requirements" until all 3 rules are met; Confirm shows "Confirm your password" when empty or "Passwords don’t match". Each field also reveals its errors after it is blurred (never while typing in a fresh field)
A valid submit calls createAccount; the button reads Creating… and is disabled until it settles

For taken@example.com, the API message appears in a red banner above the fields (.api-error) and the form stays filled. Success replaces the form with "Check your inbox" and the email address (.success)
hints: Don’t put error messages in state. Compute emailError, passwordError, confirmError with plain ifs above the return.
Show-or-not is the state: useState<Record<FieldName, boolean>>({ email: false, password: false, confirm: false }) plus submitted. Search: "mdn blur event" for onBlur.
Mark one field touched: setTouched((prev) => { return { ...prev, [field]: true }; }); (computed property name).
Checklist: PASSWORD_RULES.map((rule) => { let cls = "rule"; if (rule.test(password)) { cls = "rule is-met"; } ... }); all met: PASSWORD_RULES.every(...).

Submit: e.preventDefault(); setSubmitted(true); if (!isValid) { return; } setStatus("submitting"); createAccount(email, password).then(...).catch((err: Error) => { setApiError(err.message); setStatus("idle"); });
rubric: Errors derived, visibility in state
Blur and submit both reveal errors
Reused Field, isValidEmail and PASSWORD_RULES
No API call when invalid; button disabled while submitting (no double submit)
Server error shown without clearing the form
Status modelled as one value (idle / submitting / success)
e.preventDefault() on submit

primitives.name: e.preventDefault() on submit
primitives.example: <form onSubmit={(e) => { handleSubmit(e); }}> ... <button type="submit">Create account</button></form>
primitives.note: A form submit reloads the page by default. preventDefault() stops that so React handles it. Enter in any input also submits.

primitives.name: Calling a function stored in an object
primitives.example:
const rule = { label: 'Contains a number', test: (pw: string) => { return /\d/.test(pw); } };
rule.test('abc1')   // true
primitives.note: Objects can hold functions. Here each rule carries its own check, so the checklist is just a map calling rule.test(...).

primitives.name: trim() for "empty"
primitives.example:
'   '.trim() === ''     // true: only spaces counts as empty
' a@b.co '.trim()      // 'a@b.co'
primitives.note: Returns a new string without leading/trailing whitespace. Check emptiness on the trimmed value.

primitives.name: if / else if chain for one message
primitives.note: Only the first matching branch runs, so each field shows its most important error. Compute it every render; don’t store it.

dc18.title: Patients: master-detail
dc18.summary: A clinic’s day view. Selecting a patient on the left fetches their chart by id into the right panel, with a loading state and no stale responses.
dc18.brief:
Carepoint shows today’s patients on the left (PatientList, already loading via getPatients()) and an empty ChartPanel on the right. Rows don’t respond to clicks yet.

Read api.ts: getPatient(id) returns the full chart. Margaret’s chart is archived and always takes 1.2–1.5 s; the others take 0.3–0.7 s. So clicking Margaret then Daniel quickly is a real race. components/PatientChart.tsx (built for the printable view) already renders a full chart from a loaded PatientDetail, and components/ChartSkeleton.tsx is the loading placeholder; their CSS is in styles.css. utils/age.ts is there to reuse.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The list sets the selection and the chart reads it, so selectedId lives in App. I store the id, not the patient. ChartPanel gets patientId and has an effect on [patientId] that fetches the details. The cleanup sets cancelled = true, so when I click Daniel while Margaret is still loading, Margaret’s late answer is ignored."
requirements: Clicking a patient row selects it: light-blue background with a blue left bar (is-selected). Before any click the right panel keeps "Select a patient to view their chart."
Selecting fetches getPatient(id). While loading, the panel shows <ChartSkeleton /> (shimmer + "Loading chart…"); then <PatientChart patient={...} /> (both already exist in components/)
Click Margaret Ellison then immediately Daniel Reyes: the panel ends on Daniel and never flashes Margaret’s chart when her slow response arrives
Extend PatientChart: the meta line reads "36 y · M · MRN … · phone" using ageFrom (not the raw DOB), and an empty allergy list shows "No known allergies" (Daniel) instead of a blank area
hints: State placement: const [selectedId, setSelectedId] = useState<string | null>(null); in App. PatientList gets selectedId + onSelect.
ChartPanel effect: useEffect(() => { if (!patientId) { return; } ... }, [patientId]);
The race: search "react useEffect race condition fetch" (react.dev "You might not need an effect" → "Fetching data" shows the ignore flag).
Shape: let cancelled = false; setLoading(true); getPatient(patientId).then((data) => { if (cancelled) { return; } setPatient(data); setLoading(false); }); return () => { cancelled = true; };
Decide the panel with early returns: no id → the existing empty message, loading || !patient → <ChartSkeleton />, else <PatientChart patient={patient} />.
rubric: Selection lifted to the common parent, stored as an id
Detail fetch keyed on the id in the dependency array
Stale responses ignored via cleanup
Skeleton shown on every switch (no old chart under a new name)
Reused Avatar and ageFrom
Empty lists handled

primitives.name: Effect keyed on a prop
primitives.example:
useEffect(() => { if (!patientId) { return; } getPatient(patientId).then(...); }, [patientId]);
// click Daniel → patientId 'p2' → effect runs again
primitives.note: Every new id re-runs the effect. Return early when there is nothing to load; you cannot put a hook inside an if, but you can put an if inside the hook.
primitives.search: react useEffect fetch on prop change

primitives.name: Narrowing a nullable value
primitives.note: After an if (!x) return, TypeScript treats x as non-null for the rest of the function.

primitives.name: Callback prop to report a click
primitives.example:
<button onClick={() => { onSelect(p.id); }}>...</button>
// parent: <PatientList onSelect={(id) => { setSelectedId(id); }} />
primitives.note: The child doesn’t own the selection; it tells the parent. The parent stores the id and passes it to whoever needs it.

dc19.title: Deploy toasts
dc19.summary: A dark deploy dashboard. Show stacked success/error toasts bottom-right for each action, auto-dismissed after 3 s with proper timer cleanup.
dc19.brief:
Shipyard’s service page has three actions that already work: Deploy to staging (resolves, 0.3–0.8 s), Roll back production (always rejects with a message: change freeze), and Clear cache (instant). They show busy labels but nobody is told the result.

Read Actions in App.tsx (the TODOs mark where results arrive), api.ts, and components/Toast.tsx: it exports the ToastData type and a Toast card that only renders (no list, no position, no timer). Its CSS is in styles.css; you write the stack’s positioning.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3, and the change.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Toasts are a list in App, because they sit outside Actions and outlive it. Actions gets a notify(kind, message) prop. Each toast has an id from a useRef counter. Each Toast owns a setTimeout in an effect and clears it in the cleanup, so closing early doesn’t leave a timer behind. dismiss is wrapped in useCallback so the timers don’t restart on every render."
requirements: Deploy shows a green success toast "Deployed <commit> to staging"; Roll back shows a red error toast with the API’s message; Clear cache shows "Cache cleared for api-gateway". Render each with the existing <Toast /> inside a stack fixed bottom-right (.toast-stack: 20px from the edges, 340 wide), newest at the bottom
Each toast disappears on its own after 3 seconds. Its ✕ button removes it immediately. Timers are cleared in an effect cleanup
Removing one toast doesn’t reset the timers of the others (each toast keeps its own 3 s)

change.title: At most 3
change.html:
"Someone mashed Clear cache and the toasts covered the page."

  • Show at most 3 toasts. When a 4th arrives, the oldest one is dropped.

One line in the updater. Check that the dropped toast’s timer is cleaned up too (it is, if the timer lives in the toast’s effect).

hints: State: useState<ToastData[]>([]) in App, with import type { ToastData, ToastKind } from "./components/Toast";
Ids that don’t need a render: const nextId = useRef(1); then nextId.current += 1. Search: "react useRef".
Timer per toast: useEffect(() => { const t = setTimeout(() => { onDismiss(toast.id); }, 3000); return () => { clearTimeout(t); }; }, [toast.id, onDismiss]);

If onDismiss is a new function every render, that effect restarts every time. Search: "react useCallback". const dismiss = useCallback((id: number) => { setToasts((prev) => { return prev.filter(...); }); }, []);
Change: setToasts((prev) => { return [...prev, toast].slice(-3); });
rubric: Toast list lives above the actions; notify passed down
Stable ids (ref counter), never array index
Timer cleared in cleanup
Explained why dismiss needs to be stable
Updater form for add and remove
Change done as a one-line slice
aria-live region

primitives.name: setTimeout / clearTimeout
primitives.example:
const t = setTimeout(() => { console.log('gone'); }, 3000);
clearTimeout(t);   // cancelled: 'gone' never logs
primitives.note: setTimeout returns an id; pass it to clearTimeout to cancel. Cancelling an already-fired timer is harmless.

primitives.name: useEffect cleanup
primitives.note: The function you return runs when the component unmounts (toast closed) and before the effect runs again. Put the timer in the toast, and closing it early clears it for free.

primitives.name: useRef as a counter
primitives.note: A ref is a box that survives renders. Changing .current does not re-render, which is exactly right for an id counter.

primitives.name: Append, then keep the last N
primitives.note: Spread makes a new array with the item added. slice(-n) returns a new array of the last n items (fewer if shorter). Used for the change.

dc20.title: Files: confirm delete
dc20.summary: A cloud-files list. The trash button opens a confirm modal naming the file; Delete calls the API, shows "Deleting…", then removes the row.
dc20.brief:
Driftbox lists your files (FileList, loaded via getFiles()). Each row’s 🗑 already calls handleDeleteClick(id) in FileList, which does nothing yet.

Read api.ts (deleteFile(id) takes 0.4–1.0 s) and components/Button.tsx: it already has a danger variant and supports autoFocus and disabled. Reuse it for the modal’s buttons.

components/ConfirmDeleteModal.tsx is the static markup from the design hand-off: not rendered anywhere, no props, buttons that do nothing. Its CSS is in styles.css. Make it real.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Stretch: 5.
Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"FileList owns the files, so it also owns pendingId (which file we’re asking about; null means closed) and deleting. FileRow gets an onDelete(id) callback. A ConfirmDeleteModal component gets the name and onCancel/onConfirm, and adds a keydown listener for Escape with a cleanup. Confirm calls the API, then filters the file out and closes."
requirements: Clicking a row’s 🗑 opens the modal (turn the static ConfirmDeleteModal into one that takes props): title Delete “Q3 roadmap.pdf”? with the real file name, the warning line, Cancel (secondary) and Delete (red, danger variant)
Cancel closes without deleting. Delete calls deleteFile(id); when it resolves, the row disappears and the modal closes
While deleting, the button reads Deleting… and both buttons are disabled
Escape and clicking the backdrop close the modal without deleting. Clicking inside the panel does not close it
Focus starts on Cancel (the safe choice), the dialog has role="alertdialog" and aria-modal, and Escape is ignored while deleting. When the last file is gone, show "No files left."
hints: Store which file, not a copy: const [pendingId, setPendingId] = useState<string | null>(null); Then files.find(...) to get its name.
Render the modal only when there is a pending file: let modal = null; if (pendingFile) { modal = <ConfirmDeleteModal ... />; }
Escape: document.addEventListener("keydown", handleKey) in an effect, and remove it in the cleanup. Search: "mdn KeyboardEvent key Escape".
Backdrop only: if (e.target === e.currentTarget) { onCancel(); }
Remove after the API: deleteFile(id).then(() => { setFiles((prev) => { return prev.filter((f) => { return f.id !== id; }); }); setDeleting(false); setPendingId(null); });
rubric: Modal state is an id; name derived with find
Reused Button (danger variant)
Keydown listener cleaned up
Backdrop vs panel click handled
Deleting state prevents double delete
Row removed immutably after the API resolves
Accessibility: alertdialog, focus on Cancel

primitives.name: find() by id
primitives.example:
files.find((f) => { return f.id === 'f3'; })    // { id: 'f3', name: 'Offsite agenda.docx', ... }
files.find((f) => { return f.id === 'nope'; })  // undefined
primitives.note: Returns the first matching item, or undefined. Store only the id in state and derive the object with find.

primitives.name: filter() to remove an item
primitives.syntax: setList((prev) => { return prev.filter((x) => { return x.id !== id; }); });
primitives.note: Keeps everything except the match and returns a new array: the immutable way to delete.

primitives.name: Act after the request
primitives.note: Code after .then(...) on the next line runs immediately; code inside the callback runs when the server answers. Update the UI inside.

primitives.name: Render only when there is something
primitives.note: null in JSX renders nothing, so the modal mounts when a file is pending and unmounts (cleaning up its effects) when it is closed.
